articles.title: Tottenham v Coventry: Premier League – live
articles.summary: ⚽ Live updates from the 8pm BST kick-off ⚽ Get in touch! Share your thoughts with Daniel. Sport’s ability to ape and shape the world means it teaches us many things, often in a friendlier environment than real life.
body: Football, though, is a slightly different thing, the constant competition and the way in which teams are passed down through families installing their nature as part of our personalities, both heirloom and genetics. And within that, there’s supporting Tottenham, a relentless barrage of dark nights and false dawns delivering martyrdom to the afflicted and mirth to everyone else.

Even in context, though, a summer spend in excess of £300m, to go from fourth-bottom to bottom, is exceptional behaviour, suggesting a malaise too encoded to alleviate. But it is also the case that their performances have been better than three points from six games suggest – which might be viewed as integral to the nature of it all, or might indicate an imminent upturn.

articles.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
articles.summary: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis. When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis…
body: At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first versus third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that, whatever that was, in Istanbul – an “almost rabona,” the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote.

articles.title: Uefa gives Infantino two-week deadline to release key documents
articles.summary: Uefa's letter contained 42 questions, covering Fifa's failed private investment proposals, its Peace Prize and the fallout from Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card.
body: European governing body Uefa has told Fifa it must release key documents and answer all questions relating to its governance and decision-making by a deadline of 2 November.
At the Fifa Council on Thursday, president Gianni Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan - but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised.
In the letter seen by BBC Sport, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis said that world football's governing body had failed to address "a number of fundamental questions".
"Others remain unanswered, and the information and documentation requested have not been provided," it read.

articles.title: ‘Money and medals over safety’: Nassar judge warns gymnasts are still being failed
articles.summary: Larry Nassar’s sexual abuse crimes came to light 10 years ago. Survivors gather at World Gymnastics Championships to call for reform. The judge who sentenced the former USA Gymnastics team doctor Larry Nassar to up to 175 years in jail for the sexual abuse of more than 250 women and girls has…
body: Against the backdrop of the World Gymnastics Championships, taking place in Rotterdam this week, Judge Rosemarie Aquilina told the Guardian that human rights must be prioritised over the desire for sporting success.

“Nassar was 10 years ago and there have been very few changes that are meaningful,” said Aquilina, who insisted on all 169 impact statements being heard in her courtroom after Nasser’s guilty plea. “I’m not looking for little changes that a lot of people get credit for, I want meaningful change, a lot of meaningful changes, and we’re just not there yet, not in sports, not in life, not in the courtroom, not in the classroom or in the legislature. I have to ask why? It’s the same answer: it’s money, medals and notoriety over the safety of children, and safety is a human right, it’s not a question mark.”

Aquilina joined activists, survivors and advocates from Gymnasts for Change International (GCI) in Rotterdam, who gathered to question why the level of change has been inadequate 10 years on from Nassar’s arrest and what can be done.

articles.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
articles.summary: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win. “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner.
body: The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat to Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to a breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season.

His replacement, Davide Nicola, is a renowned survival specialist, though his most recent appointment at Cremonese ended with his dismissal last March, when the team were 18th. If Venice’s Lagoon has a deep end, then Nicola was thrown into it, beginning this latest job at home to last season’s runners-up, Napoli.

But a man whose past relegation escapes have drawn comparison with Harry Houdini could hardly be afraid of the water. Nicola’s first Venezia team sat in a patient low block, refusing to be drawn out. And when an opportunity was casually presented to them at the start of the second half, they took it.
points: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win.
“I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner.
The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th.
The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom.

articles.title: Brentford contact police after rugby ball kicked into stadium
articles.summary: Brentford say they are working with the police following a "dangerous" incident in which a rugby ball was kicked from a height towards the pitch during their Premier League game with Liverpool.
body: A video on social media shows a man standing on a rooftop near the Gtech Community Stadium, kicking a rugby ball towards the pitch while others laugh and cheer.
Another clip from inside the ground shows the rugby ball being taken away from the pitch by a member of staff as play continued.
In a statement, Brentford, who were beaten 2-1 on Saturday, said "such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful".

"The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution," the statement added.

"I remember being at the Tour de France in 2019 and I was lucky enough to be invited around the bus the morning that Matteo Trentin won the stage for the team into Gap.

articles.title: Jota 'met some demons' during long injury absence
articles.summary: Jota admits he "met some demons" during his long injury absence but believes there is no need to "rush" his return to full match fitness at Celtic.
body: The Portuguese winger, 27, sustained cruciate ligament damage in April 2025 and made his first-team return last weekend in the 2-0 win at Motherwell.
And, after coming off the bench again in Sunday's 7-1 Scottish Premiership victory at home to Hearts, Jota believes the ordeal has strengthened his character.
"I've met some demons and I've had some good talks with them," he said. "We developed a good relationship and we are all on the same table nowadays and we can laugh about everything that happened.
"If you don't grow from a situation like this, it's because you didn't learn anything.

articles.title: Australia strike late on rain-hit second day against South Africa
articles.summary: Scott Boland has taken four of South Africa's five wickets to fall, including that of Ryan Rickelton late on another rain-hit day in Gqeberha, as Australia reduced their hosts to 97-5 in the second Test.
body: After rain washed out the first two sessions of the second day, when South Africa's first innings finally resumed at 20-2 they swiftly lost a third wicket after only a couple of overs.
Boland (4-31), who had taken two wickets with consecutive deliveries on day one, added debutant Marques Ackerman caught behind for six.
Mitchell Starc (1-27) then struck to remove Matthew Breetzke (4) - also nicking off, when chasing a wide drive - to have the Proteas rocking at 40-4.
Australia were shorn of one of their four-pronged front-line pace options, with Josh Hazlewood absent on day two due to illness. He is expected to be available for the remainder of the Test.

articles.title: Sage under increasing pressure at Crystal Palace
articles.summary: Crystal Palace have no immediate plans to change their manager - but Pierre Sage is under increasing pressure following their 5-0 thrashing at Brighton on Sunday.
body: Palace find themselves 14th with seven points from seven games and Sage was unable to give assurances he had the club's full support after such a bitter defeat to their rivals.

Chairman Steve Parish recently stated the club was on "high alert" during the transitionary process from the era of Oliver Glasner into the new one under Sage, which includes a number of new players and a first Europa League campaign.
Asked after the defeat whether he would be given time to turn things around, Sage said: "I don't know.
"I just want to apologise to the fans because it's not normal to show this face for this club against this other club, and we are not at the level we expected.
